findings.text: The owner's on-screen "undefined" came from the chat view, and the view is still not fixed. `public/framework/ext/Chat/v3/ChatV3.js:156` draws every non-Prompt root as `first_words(m.text)`, and `ChatV3.js:221` does `String(text ?? "")`. Before this change a generic `Item` had no `.text`, so the screen showed "undefined". After it, a `{icon, title}` card draws as an empty, untitled note: `m.title` and `m.icon` are never drawn, and neither is `content`. `ChatList.js:65` draws a title only for a Prompt. So "the owner asked for a card and it must work" is not met on the owner's screen. Fix `note()` (and ChatList's note) to draw `icon` + `title` + `content`, and test that a card shows its title.

Any other unregistered type an agent guesses (e.g. `type:"Note"`, `"Task card"`) still becomes a generic Item, and `ChatV3.note` still renders the word "undefined" for it. The alias at `Message.js` (`Message.TYPES.Card = Message`) covers only one guess. The cause is the view's `m.text` on a member that has no `text` getter. Guard it in the view, or make Chat hydrate an unknown type as a Message.

"or a ref to an existing item" (requirements ask 3, the owner's first bullet) is not addressed anywhere: no call is named, there is no test, and neither the readme nor the brief lines mention it. `content` is a plain `List`, so `content:{add:{type:"Ref", ...}}` probably works, but it is unproven and undocumented.

The upgrade path is invisible in the main view. `ChatV3.js:60` never draws a Reply as a root, and `reply()` at `ChatV3.js:192` ignores `title`/`icon`. So "upgrading" a Reply into a card by setting its title (the readme's claim, `core/Session/Chat/readme.md` card bullet) changes nothing the owner sees. The test (`Servex/agents/card-messages.test.mjs`, step 3) only proves the data changed.

`risk.md`'s Decision says the three brief lines are "one example call, one line on upgrading an existing message, one line saying type is never needed". The lines actually added to `Servex/agents/single-voice-assistant.md:25-26` are a card example (which also says no type) and an append line. There is no upgrade line, so the record and the change disagree.

The brief line says "never a `type`", while the readme and the code alias `type:"Card"` on purpose. Both are true, but a fresh agent reading only one of them gets mixed signals. One sentence in the readme ("the alias is a safety net; write no type") would settle it.

The test writes its scratch sessions into the live store (`public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/16/.card-messages-test-*`). The dev server watches that tree, and a crash between `mkdir` and `finally` leaves a stray folder there. An OS temp dir would be safer, if `run_item` accepts one.

There is no task.jsonl in the minion folder (only `session.jsonl` with the finish line), and `requirements.md` lives in the parent's `ask3-cards-by-id/` folder. A fresh agent can continue from that folder only if it knows to look there. The finish line does name the commit, `cacdb7e07` on `worktree/qf-5`, which is not yet merged.
Verified: in the qf-5 worktree, `card-messages.test.mjs` passes 10/10, `chat-messages.test.mjs` 22/22 and `Chat.test.mjs` 26/26. The `page_tools.js` read-back change (`?? ""`) is correct and small.
